NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 7 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 25 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 23, 10:21 AM ET

George Kittle is the top-projected tight end on the Week 7 DraftKings main slate at 17.4 DraftKings points for $5,700, at Atlanta. Brock Bowers (16.9, $7,700) and Trey McBride (16.4, $7,400) are next.

Cade Otton returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 3.51 projected points per $1,000 at $3,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 23, 10:21 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 7

George Kittle, SF at ATL ($5,700)

George Kittle carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 17.4 DraftKings points at $5,700. That is 0.5 points clear of Brock Bowers. The model gives him 7.6 targets on 22.7 routes. The salary works out to 3.05 projected points per $1,000, 2nd of 15 at the position. Across 100,000 simulations Kittle averaged 17.4 points with a simulated floor of 6.6 and a ceiling of 35.8, and he holds 27% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 2.5-point favorite on the road against Atlanta, with an implied team total of 26 in a game totaled at 49.5.

Brock Bowers, LV vs LAR ($7,700)

Brock Bowers projects 2nd at the position with 16.9 DraftKings points at $7,700. The model gives him 8.0 targets on 30.1 routes. The salary works out to 2.20 projected points per $1,000, 14th of 15 at the position. Across 100,000 simulations Bowers averaged 16.9 points with a simulated floor of 6.3 and a ceiling of 34.7, and he holds 6% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 3.5-point underdog at home against the Rams, with an implied team total of 22.5 in a game totaled at 48.5.

Value: Cade Otton, TB at CAR ($3,100)

Cade Otton projects for 10.9 DraftKings points at $3,100, which works out to 3.51 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 15 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 6.4 targets on 30.6 routes. Across 100,000 simulations Otton averaged 10.9 points with a simulated floor of 2.5 and a ceiling of 26.3, and he holds 24% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Tampa Bay is a 3-point underdog on the road against Carolina, with an implied team total of 20.75 in a game totaled at 44.5.
